526:
(a) When used in this article, the following words or phrases shall have the meanings given in this section. Terms not defined herein shall have their customary dictionary definitions where not inconsistent with the context, or as set forth in a previous resolution. The term "shall" is mandatory: the word "may" is permissive. The words "structure" and "building" have the same definition. Words used in the singular include the plural and those used in the plural include the singular.
Access easement. An easement in existence on April 5, 1988.
Class I street. Street with right-of-way dedicated to a property owners' association of the subdivision involved or reserved in the name of the developer and which would allow for further street development. Possessor of the right-of-way is responsible for ongoing street maintenance including drainage, crushed stone, asphalt and concrete surface course.
Class II street. Street with right-of-way dedicated to a property owners' association of the subdivision involved or reserved in the name of the developer and which would not allow for further street development. Possessor of the right-of-way is responsible for ongoing street maintenance including drainage, crushed stone, asphalt and concrete surface course.
Public street. A street within the right-of-way owned by the state or by the county.
Site plan. A graphic illustration, two-dimensional, prepared to scale, showing accurately and with complete dimensioning, the boundaries of a lot or tract and the location of all buildings, structures, uses and principal site development features proposed for a specific lot or tract of land.
Vacation rental/tourist cabin. A unit built for the purpose of rental to guest for short periods of time.
Vacation rental/tourist cabin development. A tract of land containing two or more vacation rental cabins.
(Res. No. 2002-21, 6-4-02)
527:
(a) Development planning authority. From and after the passage of this article, the planning commission shall be the official development planning authority. The planning director is authorized to address situations where this article does not indicate a procedure, provided such action is ratified by the planning commission at the next regular meeting. No approved preliminary development plan of a vacation rental/tourist cabin development shall be recorded in the office of the clerk of the superior court of the county.
(b) Use of development plan. Property or any portion thereof that has been designated and approved as a vacation rental/tourist cabin development cannot be transferred, sold, agreed to be sold or negotiated to be sold unless such property or portion thereof meets all existing requirements and regulations then existing for the proposed use and/or subdivision of the property. The description by metes and bounds in an instrument of transfer or other document shall not exempt the transaction from penalty.
(c) Erection of buildings. One building permit may be issued in the unincorporated areas of the county before final approval of a development plan.
(d) New work. No developer shall institute or proceed with any construction work in a vacation rental/tourist cabin development before obtaining a preliminary site plan approval from the planning commission. Specifically, and without limiting the scope of this paragraph, no permit under the county's soil erosion and sediment control resolution shall be issued for land disturbance activities within the area encompassed by the development, any portion thereof, or any activity providing access to the development, until the preliminary development plan is approved.
(e) Permanent occupancy of vacation rental/tourist cabins. No vacation/tourist cabin shall be permanently occupied and no vacation rental/tourist cabin development permit shall be issued for full time residential structures. For the purposes of this subsection, a vacation rental/tourist cabin occupied for less than 31 consecutive days shall be considered non-permanent and temporary, and any occupancy greater then 31 consecutive days shall be considered permanent.
(Res. No. 2002-21, 6-4-02)
528:
(a) Pre-application review. Whenever development of a tract of land within the county is proposed for a vacation rental/tourist cabin development, the developer is urged to consult early and informally with the planning commission or its designated representative. The developer may present a sketch of plans and data showing existing conditions within the site and its vicinity and the proposed layout and development of that site and request advice and guidance concerning the project and the administrative procedures involved. No fee shall be charged for the pre-application review and no formal application shall be required.
(b) Sequence of administrative procedures. Listed below, in normal sequential order, are the generally occurring steps required to successfully complete development of a vacation rental/tourist cabin development.
(1) Pre-application review session with the field representative of the planning commission (sketch plan and general data).
(2) Obtain a copy of the county vacation rental/tourist cabin regulations.
(3) Consult with the county health department to obtain its requirements for water supply and sewage management and identify any possible water or sewage problems associated with the proposed land development.
(4) Consult with USDA Natural Resource Conservation Service for assistance in ensuring the development does not propose building sites in flood plains, flood hazard areas and that natural waterways will not be interrupted.
(5) Consult with all utility providers providing service to the development and furnish letters to each utility acknowledging that service shall be provided.
(6) Have land surveyed to obtain data for preliminary development plan and final development plan.
(7) Develop preliminary development plan with surveyors and submit to planning commission 15 days prior to the meeting at which the preliminary development plan approval is to be sought.
(8) Be prepared to accompany planning commission member(s) or their designated representative(s) to the site prior to planning commission meeting.
(9) Attend the planning commission meeting at which preliminary development plan approval is sought. No action will be taken by the planning commission unless the developer or his authorized representative is present.
(10) Obtain grading permit from the planning commission office upon approval of the preliminary development plan.
(11) Begin development work.
(12) Request inspection of land disturbance, if any by the building inspector or code compliance officer, as directed, prior to applying road surface material such as gravel or pavement and before seeding as may be required by conditions of grading permit.
(13) Complete survey work if needed.
(14) Request final on-site inspection of development by the county planning commission or their representative, prior to approval being given by the planning commission.
(15) Submit final development plan to the planning commission, or their representative. The plan must note all changes specified by the planning commission when the preliminary plan was given tentative approval.
(c) Application for preliminary plan approval. The developer shall submit to the planning commission, or its designated representative, at least 15 days prior to the next regular meeting of the planning commission, the following:
(1) A letter requesting a review and approval of the preliminary development plan, giving the name, address, and phone number of the person to whom the notice of the hearing shall be given.
(2) Seven copies of the development plan and other documents as specified in section 14-255.
(3) A preliminary plan fee as set by the county board of commissioners.
(d) Review of preliminary plan. The planning commission or its designated representative, shall check the development plan for conformance to the rules and regulations of this article and the applicant shall be afforded a hearing on the preliminary plan. Notice of time and place shall be given by the planning commission to the person designated in the letter requesting preliminary development plan review and approval.
Thereafter, the planning commission shall give tentative approval or disapproval to the preliminary plan, including a statement of the reasons for disapproval if the plan is disapproved. One copy shall be returned to the developer or his agent and three copies added to the records of the planning commission.
Tentative approval of a preliminary plan does not constitute approval of a final plan. It indicates only approval of the layout as a guide to the preparation of the final plan. Tentative approval shall expire and be null and void after a period of one year unless an extension of time is approved by the planning commission.
